# Tests for glob_match(pattern, name) implementing fnmatch.fnmatchcase semantics

# Basic literal matching
assert glob_match("abc", "abc") == True, (glob_match("abc", "abc"), True)
assert glob_match("abc", "abd") == False, (glob_match("abc", "abd"), False)
assert glob_match("abc", "ab") == False, (glob_match("abc", "ab"), False)
assert glob_match("abc", "abcd") == False, (glob_match("abc", "abcd"), False)
assert glob_match("", "") == True, (glob_match("", ""), True)
assert glob_match("", "a") == False, (glob_match("", "a"), False)

# * wildcard: matches any run including empty
assert glob_match("*", "") == True, (glob_match("*", ""), True)
assert glob_match("*", "a") == True, (glob_match("*", "a"), True)
assert glob_match("*", "abc") == True, (glob_match("*", "abc"), True)
assert glob_match("a*c", "ac") == True, (glob_match("a*c", "ac"), True)
assert glob_match("a*c", "abc") == True, (glob_match("a*c", "abc"), True)
assert glob_match("a*c", "abbc") == True, (glob_match("a*c", "abbc"), True)
assert glob_match("a*c", "ab") == False, (glob_match("a*c", "ab"), False)
assert glob_match("a*c", "abc") == True, (glob_match("a*c", "abc"), True)
assert glob_match("*a*", "a") == True, (glob_match("*a*", "a"), True)
assert glob_match("*a*", "ba") == True, (glob_match("*a*", "ba"), True)
assert glob_match("*a*", "ab") == True, (glob_match("*a*", "ab"), True)
assert glob_match("*a*", "b") == False, (glob_match("*a*", "b"), False)
assert glob_match("a*b*c", "abc") == True, (glob_match("a*b*c", "abc"), True)
assert glob_match("a*b*c", "abbc") == True, (glob_match("a*b*c", "abbc"), True)
assert glob_match("a*b*c", "abcc") == True, (glob_match("a*b*c", "abcc"), True)
assert glob_match("a*b*c", "ab") == False, (glob_match("a*b*c", "ab"), False)

# ? wildcard: matches exactly one character
assert glob_match("?", "") == False, (glob_match("?", ""), False)
assert glob_match("?", "a") == True, (glob_match("?", "a"), True)
assert glob_match("?", "ab") == False, (glob_match("?", "ab"), False)
assert glob_match("?b", "ab") == True, (glob_match("?b", "ab"), True)
assert glob_match("?b", "b") == False, (glob_match("?b", "b"), False)
assert glob_match("?b", "acb") == False, (glob_match("?b", "acb"), False)
assert glob_match("a?c", "abc") == True, (glob_match("a?c", "abc"), True)
assert glob_match("a?c", "ac") == False, (glob_match("a?c", "ac"), False)
assert glob_match("a?c", "abbc") == False, (glob_match("a?c", "abbc"), False)

# Character classes [abc]
assert glob_match("[abc]", "a") == True, (glob_match("[abc]", "a"), True)
assert glob_match("[abc]", "b") == True, (glob_match("[abc]", "b"), True)
assert glob_match("[abc]", "c") == True, (glob_match("[abc]", "c"), True)
assert glob_match("[abc]", "d") == False, (glob_match("[abc]", "d"), False)
assert glob_match("[abc]", "") == False, (glob_match("[abc]", ""), False)
assert glob_match("[abc]", "ab") == False, (glob_match("[abc]", "ab"), False)
assert glob_match("x[abc]y", "xay") == True, (glob_match("x[abc]y", "xay"), True)
assert glob_match("x[abc]y", "xdy") == False, (glob_match("x[abc]y", "xdy"), False)

# Ranges [a-z]
assert glob_match("[a-z]", "a") == True, (glob_match("[a-z]", "a"), True)
assert glob_match("[a-z]", "m") == True, (glob_match("[a-z]", "m"), True)
assert glob_match("[a-z]", "z") == True, (glob_match("[a-z]", "z"), True)
assert glob_match("[a-z]", "A") == False, (glob_match("[a-z]", "A"), False)
assert glob_match("[a-z]", "0") == False, (glob_match("[a-z]", "0"), False)
assert glob_match("[A-Z]", "A") == True, (glob_match("[A-Z]", "A"), True)
assert glob_match("[A-Z]", "Z") == True, (glob_match("[A-Z]", "Z"), True)
assert glob_match("[A-Z]", "a") == False, (glob_match("[A-Z]", "a"), False)
assert glob_match("[0-9]", "5") == True, (glob_match("[0-9]", "5"), True)
assert glob_match("[0-9]", "a") == False, (glob_match("[0-9]", "a"), False)

# Negation [!abc]
assert glob_match("[!abc]", "d") == True, (glob_match("[!abc]", "d"), True)
assert glob_match("[!abc]", "a") == False, (glob_match("[!abc]", "a"), False)
assert glob_match("[!abc]", "b") == False, (glob_match("[!abc]", "b"), False)
assert glob_match("[!abc]", "c") == False, (glob_match("[!abc]", "c"), False)
assert glob_match("[!a-z]", "A") == True, (glob_match("[!a-z]", "A"), True)
assert glob_match("[!a-z]", "m") == False, (glob_match("[!a-z]", "m"), False)
assert glob_match("[!0-9]", "a") == True, (glob_match("[!0-9]", "a"), True)
assert glob_match("[!0-9]", "5") == False, (glob_match("[!0-9]", "5"), False)

# ] immediately after [ or [! is a literal
assert glob_match("[]]", "]") == True, (glob_match("[]]", "]"), True)
assert glob_match("[]]", "a") == False, (glob_match("[]]", "a"), False)
assert glob_match("[!]a]", "a") == True, (glob_match("[!]a]", "a"), True)
assert glob_match("[!]a]", "!") == True, (glob_match("[!]a]", "!"), True)
assert glob_match("[!]a]", "b") == False, (glob_match("[!]a]", "b"), False)

# Unterminated [ is a literal [
assert glob_match("[abc", "[abc") == True, (glob_match("[abc", "[abc"), True)
assert glob_match("[abc", "abc") == False, (glob_match("[abc", "abc"), False)
assert glob_match("a[bc", "a[bc") == True, (glob_match("a[bc", "a[bc"), True)
assert glob_match("a[bc", "abc") == False, (glob_match("a[bc", "abc"), False)
assert glob_match("[", "[") == True, (glob_match("[", "["), True)
assert glob_match("[", "a") == False, (glob_match("[", "a"), False)

def glob_match(pattern, name):
    """
    Implement fnmatch.fnmatchcase semantics from scratch.
    
    Supports:
    - * : matches any run of characters (including empty)
    - ? : matches exactly one character
    - [seq] : matches any character in seq
    - [!seq] : matches any character NOT in seq
    - ] immediately after [ or [! is a literal ]
    - Unterminated [ is a literal [
    
    Matching is anchored to the whole string.
    """
    def match_here(pattern, name):
        """
        Match pattern against name, both starting at their current positions.
        Returns True if the entire remaining pattern matches the entire remaining name.
        """
        while pattern:
            c = pattern[0]
            if c == '*':
                # Skip consecutive stars
                while pattern and pattern[0] == '*':
                    pattern = pattern[1:]
                if not pattern:
                    return True
                # Try matching the rest of the pattern against every possible
                # suffix of name (including empty)
                for i in range(len(name) + 1):
                    if match_here(pattern, name[i:]):
                        return True
                return False
            elif c == '?':
                if not name:
                    return False
                pattern = pattern[1:]
                name = name[1:]
            elif c == '[':

                # Find the closing ]
                # A ] immediately after [ or [! is a literal
                i = 1
                negated = False
                if i < len(pattern) and pattern[i] == '!':
                    negated = True
                    i += 1
                # If ] is immediately after [ or [!, it's a literal ]
                if i < len(pattern) and pattern[i] == ']':
                    # This ] is a literal, so we need to find the next ]
                    i += 1
                # Now find the closing ]
                start = i
                while i < len(pattern) and pattern[i] != ']':
                    i += 1
                if i >= len(pattern):
                    # Unterminated [ is a literal [

                        return False
                    if name[0] != '[':
                        return False
                    pattern = pattern[1:]
                    name = name[1:]
                    continue
                # Extract the class content
                class_content = pattern[start:i]
                # Check if the first char in class_content is a literal ]

                # We already handled that by advancing i past it, so class_content
                # starts after that literal ] if present.

                #     # So the class includes this ] as a literal

                #         name = name[1:]
                #         continue

                #     closing_pos = pos2
                
                # Let me just re-implement this cleanly:
                pos = 1
                negated = False
                if pos < len(pattern) and pattern[pos] == '!':
                    negated = True
                    pos += 1
                
                # Check if the next character is ']'
                if pos < len(pattern) and pattern[pos] == ']':
                    # This ']' is a literal member of the class
                    # Find the actual closing ']'
                    pos += 1
                    while pos < len(pattern) and pattern[pos] != ']':
                        pos += 1
                    if pos >= len(pattern):
                        # Unterminated
                        if not name:
                            return False
                        if name[0] != '[':
                            return False
                        pattern = pattern[1:]
                        name = name[1:]
                        continue
                    class_content = pattern[1:pos]
                    closing_pos = pos
                else:
                    # Normal case
                    pos2 = pos
                    while pos2 < len(pattern) and pattern[pos2] != ']':
                        pos2 += 1
                    if pos2 >= len(pattern):
                        # Unterminated
                        if not name:

                        if name[0] != '[':

                        pattern = pattern[1:]
                        name = name[1:]
                        continue
                    class_content = pattern[pos:pos2]
                    closing_pos = pos2
                
                # Now check if name is empty

                ch = name[0]
                
                # Check if ch is in the class

                j = 0

                            if low <= ch <= high:
                                in_class = True

                        # If not a valid range, treat '-' as literal

                        j += 1

                            in_class = True
                            break
                        j += 1
                
                if negated:
                    in_class = not in_class
                
                if not in_class:
                    return False
                
                pattern = pattern[closing_pos + 1:]
                name = name[1:]

        return not name
    
    return match_here(pattern, name)
